smt-2018-geometry-tiebreaker-01.title: Ratios
smt-2018-geometry-tiebreaker-01.body:
Let $CE=2x$, $DE=5x$. Then $[BCE]=\frac12\cdot2x\cdot BC=x\cdot BC=30$. The rectangle has area $CD\cdot BC=7x\cdot BC=210$.

**Answer: 210**

smt-2018-geometry-tiebreaker-02.title: Along the space diagonal
smt-2018-geometry-tiebreaker-02.body:
The tallest cylinder lies along a space diagonal of the cube, with each end disc tucked into a corner. Near a vertex the cube is cut by a plane perpendicular to the diagonal in an equilateral triangle; the end disc (radius $3$) is the incircle of that triangle, so the triangle has inradius $3$, circumradius $6$ and side $6\sqrt3$. The three edges from the corner to the triangle's vertices then have length $\frac{6\sqrt3}{\sqrt2}=3\sqrt6$, so the distance of the plane from the corner is $\sqrt{(3\sqrt6)^2-6^2}=3\sqrt2$. The height is the space diagonal minus two such caps: $12\sqrt3-2\cdot3\sqrt2=12\sqrt3-6\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $12\sqrt3-6\sqrt2$**

smt-2018-geometry-tiebreaker-03.title: Area split
smt-2018-geometry-tiebreaker-03.body:
By Heron, $s=12$ and the area is $\sqrt{12\cdot5\cdot4\cdot3}=12\sqrt5$. The triangle is acute, so a semicircle with its diameter on one side can touch the other two sides $s_1,s_2$ tangentially. Splitting the triangle from the center into two triangles with height $r$ over $s_1,s_2$ gives $\frac r2(s_1+s_2)=12\sqrt5$, so $r=\frac{24\sqrt5}{s_1+s_2}$, largest when $s_1+s_2=7+8=15$ (diameter on the side $9$): $r=\frac{24\sqrt5}{15}=\frac{8\sqrt5}{5}$.

**Answer: $\frac{8\sqrt5}{5}$**
